## Overview

The Digitize API offers authoritative data about protected areas, outdoor recreation rules, legal mandates, and wildlife sensitivities. This OpenAPI description powers the interactive documentation on our site—use it to inspect every endpoint and understand the usable parameters.

The API is read-only and available to everyone.

Regular maintenance window: Tuesdays, 09:00-11:00 (CET/CEST). Service interruptions may occur during this time.

**Base URL:** `/api/v2`
**Status:** Stable

## Hostname Migration Notice

The API is now available under `https://platform.digitizetheplanet.org/api/v2`. The previous `https://content.digitizetheplanet.org/api/v2` path remains supported for a transition period.

## Data and Licensing

Unless a payload states otherwise, data is released under **[CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)**. While the data is free to use we appreciate being cited as the source. Geospatial responses expose `license` and `source`. Images expose `license` and `copyright_holder`. Legal documents and rule records come directly from protected-area authorities.

All geometries use **EPSG:4326** (WGS84). Geometry coordinates are rounded to 7 decimal places to keep payloads compact and avoid precision that exceeds practical GPS and WGS84 accuracy (see the GeoJSON spec guidance on coordinate precision: [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7946#section-11.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7946#section-11.2)).

## Usage Guidelines

We follow a fair-use policy. There is no enforced rate limit, yet we ask clients to stay within reasonable request volumes, cache responses, and use the `fields` selector to avoid over-fetching. Honor attribution whenever a dataset’s `license` requires it. No personal data flows through this API.

## Technical Notes

### Time semantics

System and audit timestamps in API responses are expressed in **UTC**. Date-based filters over those timestamps also use **UTC** day boundaries.
